local_divergence: Rebranded: the plugin is named browser-companion, the toolset and skill namespace follow it, and every Qubit-facing identifier is rebranded. Page-supplied protocol ids (qubit.browser.turn.v2, qubit.browser.context.v1) are renamed in this copy and MUST match whatever the extension front end ships before the two halves can talk.

The HTTP readiness/context/control routes are absent: Qubit exposes no register_platform_handler seam to plugins, so this port is tool-only and reports its state through browser_context_status instead.

The hook authorizes a tool call by handing it a one-shot lease; the port keeps that lease (contextvars plus a runtime-identity table) but keys it on the native hook payload Qubit actually sends (session_id / turn_id / task_id as keyword fields).

Fail-soft: with no browser context attached (and no extension route to upload one) every context tool answers {"available": false, "reason": "Browser context unavailable."}; that is the shipped steady state of this port, not a defect.
